claims.text: The mammalian circulatory system is a closed circulation: the blood stays inside the heart and blood vessels (arteries, capillaries and veins) and is not pumped out into open spaces around the cells. The system has three parts: the heart, which acts as the pump, the blood vessels, which carry the blood, and the blood, which is the fluid tissue that is transported.

claims.text: Haemoglobin is a protein made of four polypeptide chains, each with a haem group that contains one iron(II) ion. Each haem group can bind one oxygen molecule, so one haemoglobin molecule can carry up to four: Hb + 4O₂ ⇌ HbO₈ (oxyhaemoglobin). Where the partial pressure of oxygen is high, as in the lungs, the reaction goes to the right; where it is low, as in respiring tissues, oxyhaemoglobin releases oxygen.
